headline: Funding flows. Satellites sell. Propulsion evolves.
deck: This week, the space sector sees a shift towards satellite sales and propulsion advancements.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, cash rules again
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, as the DoD continues to push for enhanced space security measures. With defense budgets tightening, it's clear that the cash is flowing where the government feels the pressure.
stories.soWhat: In an industry where innovation often takes a backseat, cash is still king, and True Anomaly's raise signals a preference for proven capabilities over untested ideas.

stories.head: Earth observation satellites outpace telecom in Europe
stories.body: European space industry sales have shown a robust rebound, with Earth observation satellites surpassing telecom sales for the first time. This shift reflects a growing demand for data-driven insights over mere connectivity, as companies and governments alike prioritize environmental monitoring and disaster response. The numbers suggest that seeing is indeed believing.
stories.soWhat: It's a telling sign that the market is valuing actionable intelligence over traditional communication, which could reshape investment strategies across the sector.

stories.head: Parabilis tests hybrid propulsion for cubesats
stories.body: Parabilis is testing a hybrid propulsion system aimed at maneuverable cubesats, backed by support from the Space Force. This move not only highlights the competitive landscape in small satellite propulsion but also indicates a strategic pivot towards more agile and responsive satellite capabilities. The stakes are high as companies scramble to keep pace.
stories.soWhat: With the Space Force's backing, Parabilis is signaling that maneuverability in space is the new frontier, and those who can't adapt may find themselves grounded.

watchlist.title: Watch for more satellite funding rounds
watchlist.body: As Earth observation sales soar, expect more venture capital to flow into satellite startups looking to capitalize on this trend.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser launch timeline
watchlist.body: With its DoD variant clearing design review, the next steps for Sierra Space could set a new benchmark for reusable spacecraft.

watchlist.title: Implications of FCC's Reflect Orbital approval
watchlist.body: The approval of Reflect Orbital's satellite could lead to further regulatory scrutiny of satellite deployments that impact astronomical observations.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension insights
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension suggests that the government remains committed to data-centric operations, reinforcing Palantir's position in defense contracts.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
